title: Node coverage counts a node only when it actually ran
description: The coverage pin reads nodeId off each span and adds it to the executed set with no status check, so a node whose span ended failed still counts as covered -- and the commit node, refused FAIL_CLOSED under the shipped noop mechanism, is exactly such a node. The committed node-coverage figure is therefore true as REACHED and weaker than it reads as EXERCISED. Correct the rule and restate the figure.

successCriteria.description: coverage.test.ts counts a node as executed only when it has at least one span with status ok.

The corrected rule is proven by mutation in both directions: a node whose only span ended failed no longer counts, and a node that gains an ok span begins to count -- both failing the pin when the NEVER_EXECUTED list is not updated to match.

The NEVER_EXECUTED list is updated to whatever the corrected rule actually yields, and each entry still carries a claim about WHY the node is unreachable, with any claim that stopped being true rewritten rather than left standing.
docs/pge-graph.md restates the node-coverage figure under the corrected rule, records the previous figure, and states plainly that the previous rule counted reached-but-refused nodes as covered.

The recorded reason for each unreachable node is re-verified against the code rather than carried forward -- in particular the claim about why synthesize is unreachable, which the analysis behind this spec flagged as possibly misattributed.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Making any node newly reachable -- executing commit and finalize under a durable checkpoint mechanism is the next spec.
Lowering the coverage floor to accommodate the corrected, likely smaller number.
stopConditions: The corrected figure falls far enough that the golden dataset no longer meaningfully covers the graph -- stop and report the number rather than adjusting the rule to protect it.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
assumptions: VERIFIED: src/pge/golden/coverage.test.ts reads `nodeId` off each span and adds it to the executed set with NO status check (the loop around :108-110). A node whose only span ended `failed` therefore counts as covered.

VERIFIED: `commit` is refused FAIL_CLOSED under the autopilot noop mechanism yet still opens a span — so it is exactly such a node, and the committed '39 of 44' figure counts at least one node that never ran its body. The figure is true as REACHED and weaker than it reads as EXERCISED.

CHANGED SINCE THE FIGURE WAS TAKEN: sprint 7 added a sixth replay case (replay-plan-clarify-rounds-exhausted) and a new specDraft channel; graphVersion is 1.4.0 and the node count may or may not still be 44. Re-derive every number from the committed artifact and the executed cases; do not carry 39 or 44 forward as literals.

EVALUATOR FINDING from sprint 7, worth acting on here: the recorded reason for `synthesize` may be MISATTRIBUTED. The committed comment says it sits behind route_after_eval's rework/partial labels needing a non-pass evaluate_global. An earlier analysis found instead that rework_route's dispatch set is always empty (nothing in the graph ever writes `abandoned`), so reworkRounds can never reach 2 and the `partial` label is dead code. Verify which is true in the CODE and record the true one — each NEVER_EXECUTED entry is a CLAIM, and a wrong claim that passes is worse than a missing one.
NFR0: no gate may be weakened. If the corrected rule lowers the coverage figure, that is the honest number — do not relax the rule to protect it.
generatorNotes: The change itself is small: src/pge/golden/coverage.test.ts:108-110 reads nodeId and ignores status. The judgement is in sc-9-3 and sc-9-5. Each NEVER_EXECUTED entry is a CLAIM about why something cannot be reached, and the two-directional pin exists so a claim that dies fails the build rather than ageing into a lie -- so when the corrected rule moves a node into the list, write the real reason rather than reusing a neighbour's. Re-read the reason recorded for synthesize specifically: the analysis behind this spec found evidence that it is unreachable because rework_route's dispatch set is always empty, not because failing paths settle earlier. Verify which is true and record the true one.
evaluatorNotes: Verify sc-9-2 by mutating in both directions yourself; a pin that only catches one direction is half a pin, and this repository's own standard says a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate. For sc-9-5, do not accept a restated reason at face value -- trace it in the code. Check that the documented figure and the test's own floor agree; a document claiming a number the test does not enforce is the exact failure this sprint is correcting.
completionNote: All 6 criteria met on iteration 1. Coverage rule now requires status 'ok'; the figure fell 39/44 -> 38/44 and `commit` joined NEVER_EXECUTED (6 entries). The evaluator RE-DERIVED 38/44 with its own executor script rather than trusting the test, and confirmed commit's spans are status 'interrupted' with errorClass FailClosed — NOT 'failed' as this contract's own assumption worded it; the generator measured rather than carried the wording forward. SYNTHESIZE: neither candidate explanation was right. The true mechanism, independently traced by the evaluator through gates.ts, sprint-fanout.ts, supervisor.ts, the artifact and the interpreter: reduce_sprints refuses admission while any branch is failed/abandoned (re-dispatching instead), so evaluate_global is reached only once EVERY branch is succeeded, which makes rework_route's dispatch set always empty, so reworkRounds can never reach 2 and route_after_eval's partial branch is dead code by construction. The sprint-7 'abandoned is never written' theory was right-conclusion-wrong-mechanism. SECONDARY: the file's blanket claim that every entry is a structural block was already false for critique and rework_route — both are closable by a missing scenario — and was corrected in place rather than by adding a case (out of scope). Suite 6897 -> 6902.
